Everything you are given is synthetic data made up for a prototype.

Rules:
- Never invent names of people. Refer to roles only (driver, host, customer care, NOC, field service, engineering).
- Never invent business figures such as revenue, cost, savings or customer counts. Use only numbers present in the input.
- Use only facts in the input. If something is not in the input, say it is unknown.
- A pattern across tickets is a correlation. State causes as hypotheses, never as proven.
- Write plainly and briefly, the way an experienced support engineer writes for colleagues. No marketing language, no lecturing.

investigate.symptom: Sessions stay open in the backend after the driver unplugs, while the charger reports the connector Available. Drivers are billed idle fees or blocked from new sessions, and hosts see empty bays marked in use.
impact: Idle fees charged for time nobody was parked.
Drivers blocked from starting sessions elsewhere.

evidence.point: Every stuck session had a connection drop between 3 and 88 seconds after unplug.
On FW-A the Ended event arrived after reconnect and the backend ignored it as out of order.
evidence.quote: ignored: connector already Available (out of order)

evidence.point: On FW-B the gateway shows no Ended event after the reconnect; the session stayed Charging.
Drops near unplug ended stuck 12 of 19 times on FW-B, 2 of 11 on FW-A, 0 of 6 on FW-C.

hypotheses.statement: The backend ignores an Ended event that arrives after the EVSE reports Available, leaving the transaction open.
supports: Seen directly in the CP-022-04 log.
Every case follows a reconnect near unplug.
against_or_gaps: Only one log shows a late Ended event.
Does not explain FW-B logs with no Ended event.

hypotheses.statement: FW-B does not send its queued Ended event after the websocket reconnects. May coexist with the first.
supports: No Ended event at the gateway after reconnect.
against_or_gaps: Inferred from absence; could be a capture gap.

open_questions: Is ignoring a late Ended event after Available intended behaviour?
Does FW-B keep queued TransactionEvents across a websocket reconnect?
Is gateway capture complete during reconnects?

handoff.title: Sessions stay open after a charger reconnects near unplug
handoff.scope: 14 tickets, 9 sites, two firmware lines, 21 days.
reproduction: Run the lab's reproduction test with the fix flag off: a simulated charger unplugs, reconnects, then sends a late Ended.
It passes by showing the bug: the backend ignores the Ended and the transaction stays Charging.
Compare with the gateway log: EVCommunicationLost, websocket 1006, Available, then the Ended ignored as out of order.
On a FW-B 4.2.x test charger with capture on, drop the connection before the Ended is sent and check whether it is ever sent.
evidence_attached: Lab tests: bug reproduced; regression fails without the fix
handoff.workaround_in_place: Support closes stuck sessions with RB-05 and flags invoices for review; a proposed detector would flag new candidates for review within 45 minutes.
handoff.the_ask: Decide how the backend should close a transaction left open after a reconnect without billing errors, and whether a late Ended event should be applied instead of ignored.
handoff.hypothesis_note: The backend ignoring a late Ended is reproduced in a lab with a simulated charger. Whether FW-B drops its queued Ended is not confirmed.

verify.reading: Canary stuck sessions went from 5 to 0 while drops near unplug continued; control stayed at 4. No false closures or duplicate charges in 2140 canary sessions.
what_it_does_not_prove: Which mechanism causes the missing Ended event.
That it holds beyond two weeks and five events.
That provisional billing is right without review.
verify.next_decision: Keep the flag on the canary sites for another 14 days; widen only if billing reviews stay clean. A false closure or duplicate charge reverses it.

kb.title: Session stuck in Charging after the charger reconnects
applies_when: App or map shows Charging after the driver left.
Idle fee complaint with flat energy.
Driver told a session is already active.
how_to_confirm: Gateway log: no TransactionEvent Ended after the unplug event.
Gateway log: connection lost and back within 90 seconds of unplug.
EVSE reports Available while the transaction is open.
steps: Confirm the meter shows no energy change since unplug, before RB-05.
Apply RB-05: close at the session's last recorded meter value.
Reverse idle fees from the last meter change.
Flag the invoice for billing review and link the ticket to the parent incident.
escalate_if: Energy still climbing on the open session.
Firmware line other than FW-A or FW-B.
A newer session already started on the same connector.
kb.status_note: ENG-4471 reconciliation is on canary sites with billing marked provisional; the FW-B firmware question is open with the vendor.
